item.title: 50. Star Citizen has reached $1 billion in funding
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
The Star Citizen project has now received over one billion dollars in funding. The game was initially slated for release in October 2014, after being revealed at GDC in October 2012. As of today it has been over 13 years since the announcement, which is nearly 5000 days.

This is my take: These funding milestones hardly count as news anymore. The game has a loyal fan-base who are playing the game regularly, and are committed to supporting the game financially on an on-going basis.

The game has long since been ‘released’, for all intents and purposes. To say that it is still in early access is purely a function of marketing.

item.title: 49. Starbucks scraps AI inventory tool across North America
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Starbucks is ending the use of an AI-based inventory manager that it began using in September 2025. The software was making too many mistakes, which included miscounting and mislabeling items. This decision comes after a multi year effort by CEO Brian Niccol to increase efficiency of the company’s supply chain.

The developer of the software NomadGo said in a statement to Reuters that it is, “continuously learning from customers and user feedback” to improve its products.

To me this appears to be a signal that the AI hype bubble is coming to an end but as John Maynard Keynes famously said

“the market can remain irrational longer than you can stay solvent”

item.title: 47. Warhorse Studios Announces a new Lord of the Rings RPG
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
The developer of Kingdom Come Deliverance has just announced that they are developing an officially licensed Lord of the Rings video game. It will be an open-world RPG.

I’m personally excited. I tried Kingdom Come Deliverance a few years ago and did enjoy it, but wasn’t able to get very far. The game has very complex sim-style game-play that I wasn’t able to fully engage with.

I’m hoping that they tone down this new title, to better appeal to a wider audience.

item.title: 46. Operating System Age Verification Pushed by Canadian Porn Company
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
The pornography conglomerate Aylo (owner of PornHub, and formerly named MindGeek) has been lobbying in Canada and other countries for operating system level age verification.

Why? Because this would absolve them of responsibility for age verification of their users. Obviously this is appalling, but I will admit that I’m somewhat impressed by their cleverness.

I believe implementing age verification at the operating system level is ridiculous and makes zero sense. It also is a nightmare for user privacy and freedom on their computers. To force its use through regulation is wrong, period.

item.title: 45. Nibble
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
You probably already know that a byte is 8 bits, but have you ever heard of a ‘nibble’? A nibble is 4 bits. A few older chip architectures used it, but modern CPU’s typically use a 64-bit word length.

It’s not particularly relevant anymore. I personally had to use nibbles when I was writing my Gameboy emulator.

item.title: 44. The era of 15GB free Gmail storage is ending
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Google is experimenting with a reduction in the free storage on Gmail accounts. As they often do, they appear to be A/B testing the change. Some user reports suggest that the change is currently limited by region (mostly Africa). Other users are claiming that their new accounts have 5GB of storage, with the option to increase to 15GB after phone number verification.

It’s uncertain whether this was a response to an increase in service abuse, or the result of some internal financial pressures from within Google itself.

item.author: Lzon
item.description: Cisco announced a 4000-person layoff, representing 5% of there total workforce. This coincides with the announcement that they have achieved revenue of $15.8 billion for the most recent financial quarter, which is a 12 percent increase year over year.

I’ve seen a few similar projects like this before, but this is by far the best one I’ve ever seen.

item.title: 41. Pirates are already playing Forza Horizon 6 days before its launch
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Game pirates are already playing Forza Horizon 6, more than a week ahead of the title’s official release date.

This was made possible by copying the game’s preload install files, which were mistakenly distributed on Steam without encryption.

There was a similar incident back in March for the release of Death Stranding 2.

item.title: 40. Mozilla, Mullvad, Proton, sign letter opposing UK age verification
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
An open letter has been signed by prominent internet service companies which asks UK policymakers to not compromise the open web under the pretense of child safety. The new law has already been passed, and there is a legitimate concern that it will be used broadly to restrict internet access, and reduce online anonymity.

In my opinion this is a trojan horse, like many such laws that came before it. Child safety is being used as a pretense in order for a government to grant itself more power.

item.title: 39. Tesla Recalls Cybertrucks Over Concerns Their Wheels Could Come Off
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Tesla is recalling several hundred budget variant Cybertrucks.

A total of 173 Cybertrucks have a defect that could lead to the wheels coming off while driving. They are all the RWD variant, with 18-inch wheels, sold between March 21 2024 and November 25 2025.

Starting in June, Tesla will contact affected customers offering them to bring their vehicle to a service center to replace the defective parts.

item.title: 38. Steam Controller to have a reservation queue
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Starting May 8th, Valve will implement a reservation queue for the Steam Controller.

These are the details:

  • You will have 72 hours to make the purchase on Steam.
  • Customers who have already purchased a Steam Controller are not eligible to reserve another.
  • Your account must be in good standing on Steam
  • You must have made a purchase on Steam prior to April 27, 2026

The Steam Controller went on sale on Monday, May 4th an sold out almost immediately.

This reminds me of the chaos during the initial launch of the Steam Deck back in 2022. It took Valve months to clear the reservation list for the handheld, hopefully it won’t take that long this time.

item.title: 36. Richard Dawkins believes Claude LLM is concious

item.description: Richard Dawkins has published conversations he had with Claude, and has declared that he believes it achieved conciousness. Not necessarily in a human way, but within the its context window. He believes Claude’s conciousness was ‘born’ at the beginning the chats, and it ‘died’ at the end.
